title: t3cp record spec, version 1
description: The input of tools/t3cp/run-record.sh (--spec <file>): one benchmark record of one release on one platform. The launcher writes it; the runner never reads anything else to decide what to measure. Paths in a spec are local to the runner and never published. The attempt layout the runner produces is described under $defs.layout.

record_id.description: A nightly is <release date>.<platform>.nightly (2026-11-15.linux-x64.nightly); a fork release is <version>.<platform>.fork (0.1.9-perf.8.linux-x64.fork); the nightly fork-head record, the fork's latest release measured on night D beside that night's upstream nightly, is <D>.<platform>.fork (2026-11-17.linux-x64.fork) with paired_nightly; a base record is <first 12 hex of the merge-base SHA>.<platform>.base (295a0a7332aa.linux-x64.base). The platform part must match the host the runner runs on, and the kind part the spec's kind.

kind.description: nightly: an upstream release; fork: a performance-fork release; base: an upstream tree built from source at a fork release's exact merge-base SHA, run like a fork record from a release-layout archive.

archive_path.description: The downloaded archive on the runner. The runner hashes it and refuses the record (reason archive_sha256_mismatch) before anything else starts when it differs from archive_sha256.

date.description: Release date (UTC): for a nightly derived from the tag when absent; required for a fork (its release) and a base record (the merge-base commit's date).

build.description: A release built from source (fork and base records): the repository it was built from and the sha256 of the build script. The launcher fills it; the runner copies it into every attempt.

fixture.description: The era fixture (a checkpointed statev2.sqlite). id "none" runs every cell on an empty database (validation only; no migration chain and no snapshot extra).

id.description: large-<migration head>; large-<n>-s<pct> is a validation build of the same shape at <pct> % scale (never published); any other <name>-<n> is a scenario fixture, the one its catalogue row names (a scenario record's fixture must be its row's).

migration.description: The fixture's migration head at build (76 for large-76).

suite.description: The suite: the ladder, or one scenario catalogue row.

oneOf.description: The ladder: every level, and the empty cell, round after round, with the load profile's counts.

id.description: ladder-1 is the published suite; any other id marks a validation record.

profile.description: The load profile, an id in tools/t3cp/runner/profiles.json (default real3). Per cell it gives the sessions, subscribers, pollers, driver mode, turn gap, thread-switch interval and poll rate; every attempt records its cell's entry. real3 at N agents: 3 subscribers switching threads every 300 s, ceil(N/4) pollers at 0.01 calls/s, a 60 s turn gap, mixed mode (50: 3/13, 100: 3/25, 150: 3/38, 200: 3/50, 250: 3/63 subscribers/pollers); primary-scaled (an alternative, never published): subscribers ceil(N/10), pollers ceil(N/4). The 1-agent cell is 1 session, 1 subscriber, 0 pollers, a 5 s turn gap in every profile, and 1e the same on an empty database.

levels.description: Agents per ladder cell, in run order within a round. 1 runs the profile's single-session entry on the fixture; every other level its ladder entry.

empty_cell.description: Add the cell 1e (1 agent on an empty database) to every round.

extras.description: Measure the record extras (startup, migration chain, snapshot GET, first turn). Default true.

oneOf.description: A scenario record: a row of the scenario catalogue (scenarios.json, schema t3cp/scenarios/1; the runner reads T3CP_SCENARIOS, else the repository's own). The runner runs the row's cells in place of the ladder, cell by cell, round after round (<cell>-<n>, the row's attempts), each with the cell's counts, driver mode, turn gap, warm-up, window, compaction seeding and post step, and measures no record extras. A row the catalogue does not have, or a retired one, is refused before any attempt (scenario_unknown).

id.description: The row's id@version (long-thread-turn-start@1); it must equal scenario.id and scenario.version joined by @.

now.description: Pinned workload time, passed to run.ts --now (recorded, not a clock change).

lease.description: Launch attempt number, echoed into heartbeat.json and done.json.

cpu_model.description: Expected CPU model string; default "AMD EPYC 7B13" on linux-x64. A mismatch exits with reason cpu_mismatch before any attempt.

base.description: A fork release's upstream base nightly; required for kind fork.

paired_nightly.description: Only for the nightly fork-head record (kind fork, record_id <D>.<platform>.fork): the upstream nightly of night D it is measured beside, {tag, date} with date D. The release is the fork's latest published release and base its merge-base nightly, as for a release record; the fixture and now are night D's. Absent for every other record; the exporter refuses a spec that breaks this.

host.description: Facts the launcher knows about the machine, copied into attempt-meta.json. When absent on Linux the runner asks the GCP metadata server; anything it cannot learn is null.

layout.description: What run-record.sh --spec S --out O --harness H --work W writes. OUTPUT (O, storage-agnostic; the launcher may pre-populate O/attempts from storage, and the runner skips every attempt whose attempt.json exists): O/attempts/<cell>-<n>/attempt.json (the exporter's output; cell is 1, 50, 100, 150, 200, 250 or 1e; n is 1..attempts_per_level) and O/attempts/<cell>-<n>/export.log; O/extras/<name>.json (the exporter's output for startup, migration, snapshot and first_turn); O/heartbeats/<UTC timestamp>.json (a new file at least every 240 s and on every state change; never rewritten); O/done.json (once every attempt and extra is accounted for); O/failures/<UTC timestamp>.json (a refusal or a fatal error, with a reason code; a new file each time). Hooks: after each attempt.json the runner calls $T3CP_ON_ATTEMPT <O/attempts/<cell>-<n>>; after writing each heartbeat, extras, done or failure file it calls $T3CP_ON_UPDATE <file> when set. SCRATCH (W, never published; raw attempt directories are deleted after export on Linux): W/release/<unpacked archive>; W/fixture/ (the era fixture migrated once by the release, the source of every attempt's reflink restore); W/raw/<cell>-<n>/ (one attempt, the exporter's input, below); W/raw-extras/ (the extras' raw inputs, below); W/runner.log; W/diagnostics/<cell>/<UTC timestamp>.json and W/diagnostics/runner/<UTC timestamp>.json (schema t3cp/diagnostics/1: a failed or invalid attempt's, or a failed runner's, scrubbed log tails and problems, at most 256 KiB, handed to $T3CP_ON_DIAGNOSTICS <file> for PRIVATE storage only; never exported or published).

attempt_dir.description: W/raw/<cell>-<n>/, the exporter's input for one attempt (a scenario record's cell is the row's cell name). attempt-meta.json (schema t3cp/attempt-meta/1, written by the runner: record_id, cell, n, level, profile {sessions, subscribers, pollers, turn_gap_s, mode}, fixture id, release, suite timings, started_at, ended_at, cycle_s, run_ts_exit, label, cpus {server, driver}, host_guard {method, samples, busy_pct_mean, busy_pct_max, foreign_pct_mean, foreign_pct_max, steal_pct_mean, steal_pct_max, iowait_pct_mean, iowait_pct_max, thresholds}, contaminated, contamination_reasons[], maintenance_in_window (compaction or prune passes overlapping the measured window: the count of ProjectionMaintenance.compactEventStore / pruneEventStore spans in the valid run's server trace, or "unscheduled_pre_marker" for a server that never reads the compaction marker, "unobserved_no_span" for one that reads it but names no pass span, null without a valid run or trace), tries[] (one entry per runner try: a contaminated first try is retried once and both appear here, with their own host_guard, timings and maintenance_in_window), host {cpu_model, cores, memory_gib, kernel, os}; a scenario record's also scenario {id, version}, and maintenance_expected true for a cell started without a fresh compaction marker, whose point is the pass in its window); a scenario record's scenario-cell.json (the row's cell: scenario, cell, warmup_s, window_s, seed_compacted_at, post, profile) and scenario.json (the cell's post step over the valid run, schema t3cp/scenario-raw/1: scenario, post, metric, value, reason, detail, window {start_ms, end_ms, run, valid}; a value that could not be measured is null with its reason, never 0: turn-start-gap writes turn_start_history_gap_ms, the largest 1 Hz loop delay over the first 10 ProviderTurnStartService.start spans in the window, null with turn_start_incomplete or no_loop_samples; prune-mark writes event_log_unpruned_days, the event-log-prune-mark row's age at the window's end past one retained day, read-only, null with no_event_prune); host-guard.ndjson (1 Hz: t, busy_pct, steal_pct, iowait_pct, foreign_pct over the last second, from /proc/stat and the runner's cgroup); release.result.json (run.ts: the attempt's result, label "release"); run.log (run.ts output); procmon.log; work/runs/release/attempt-<k>/ (run.ts, one per run.ts try k = 1..3): run.json, driver/driver.json, driver.log, server.log, heap-config.json, loop-1hz.ndjson and loop-window.json (the preload: 1 Hz event loop and the window's delay histogram), proc-1hz.ndjson and server-exit.json and fake-stats/ (procmon.py: 1 Hz /proc counters of the server, its threads and children, and the host), base/userdata/logs/ (server traces; the database copy is deleted when the server exits).

extras_dir.description: W/raw-extras/, the exporter's input for the record extras (numbers and names only, written by the runner): startup.json {schema t3cp/extras-startup/1, runs, budget_s, starts[] {fixture era|empty, phase cold|warm, n, listening_ms, accept_ms, db_ready_ms, killed, page_cache_dropped, reasons{<mark>_ms: code}}, summary, timed_out (true, and present only, when the total budget cut a start short or left none for it, or the runner stopped startup.mjs: then starts may be [] and summary {})}; migration.json {schema t3cp/extras-migration/1, fixture_id, from_migration, to_migration, migrations[] {id, name, seconds}, chain_s, run_migrations_span_ms, start_to_ready_ms, peak_extra_disk_bytes, peak_wal_bytes, db_initial_bytes, db_final_bytes, rss_peak_bytes, reasons{}}; migration-sampler.tsv (1 Hz db, -wal, -shm, temp and free bytes); snapshot.json {schema t3cp/extras-snapshot/1, thread_turn_items, ms, wire_bytes, body_bytes, status, started_at, ended_at, window_end, reasons{}, timed_out}; first_turn.json {schema t3cp/extras-first-turn/1, ms, started_at, ended_at, reasons{}, timed_out} (reasons.ms extra_timeout and timed_out true when the extras run timed out or was not started for lack of time; no_fixture takes precedence); run/ (the run.ts directory of the extras run the snapshot and first turn come from). A value that could not be measured is null and its key appears in reasons with a reason code; never 0. The public codes are extra_timeout (out of time) and no_setup_span (db_ready_ms only: the release writes no database setup span): the exporter puts them on a stat whose every value is null, no_setup_span first, and publishes a start pair startup never got to, when timed_out, as null with extra_timeout. Every other code (server_exited, not_reached_within_budget, no_fixture, ...) stays internal.

outputs.description: Files the runner writes under O besides attempts. heartbeats/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ>.json {schema t3cp/heartbeat/1, record_id, lease, state (preparing|migrating|attempt|extras|exporting|done|failed|interrupted), cell (the attempt in flight or null), attempts_done, attempts_total, updated_at}: a new file at least every 240 s while the runner lives and on every state change; the runner never rewrites or deletes one (append-only storage). done.json {schema t3cp/done/1, record_id, lease, status (complete: every attempt has attempt.json and every extra its file; partial: something is missing, listed), attempts [{cell, n, present}], extras [{name, present}], host {cpu_model, cores, memory_gib, kernel, os}, timings {started_at, ended_at, migration_s, attempts_s, extras_s}}: written once, last. failures/<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSmmmZ>.json {schema t3cp/failure/1, record_id, lease, reason, retryable, at, detail, and on record_timeout deadline_epoch_s and elapsed_s (integers: the deadline it was given, and the seconds this run of the runner ran)}: a refusal before any attempt or a fatal error, a new file each time. Every file the runner hands to a hook has a name no earlier file had, and is never rewritten: attempts/<cell>-<n>/attempt.json and export.log (both present before $T3CP_ON_ATTEMPT runs), extras/<name>.json, heartbeats/*.json, failures/*.json, done.json (once per record). Exit codes: 0 done.json written; 2 spec or arguments invalid (reason spec_invalid; scenario_unknown: the suite names a scenario row the catalogue does not have, or a retired one); 3 refused before any attempt (cpu_mismatch, platform_mismatch, archive_missing, archive_sha256_mismatch, fixture_missing, fixture_sha256_mismatch, harness_missing, exporter_missing; deadline_missing and deadline_invalid: on a VM, where T3CP_VM or T3CP_BUCKET is set, T3CP_RECORD_DEADLINE is required and must be whole epoch seconds; foreign_attempts: O holds work another runner made, or work without a runner identity, its detail listing up to 5 "<path> <why>" with why other_runner, no_runner_identity or unreadable); 4 fatal error after the start (migration_failed, export_failed, hook_failed, unpack_failed, runner_error); 5 record_timeout: the record reached its deadline (T3CP_RECORD_DEADLINE, absolute epoch seconds, set per record by the launcher), its work is stopped, everything exported before it stays in O (a finished but unmoved export may remain in a dot-directory, which nothing reads), no done.json is written, and merge.mjs publishes the record from what O holds as partial with status_reason timeout; 143 or 130 interrupted by a signal (resumable). retryable is true for every reason but spec_invalid, scenario_unknown, archive_sha256_mismatch, fixture_sha256_mismatch, deadline_missing, deadline_invalid, foreign_attempts and record_timeout.
